title: CS-05 Reopen Rate: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The Reopen Rate figure is produced under different accounting rules - reopens divided by all closed cases, which dilutes a quality signal that is specifically about AI closures - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is cases reopened within 72 hours after an AI closure; denominator is cases closed by the AI in the window.
The dictionary entry for 'Reopen Rate' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: cases reopened by the customer within 72 hours of an AI closure divided by AI-closed cases
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: reopens divided by all closed cases, which dilutes a quality signal that is specifically about AI closures
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: no AI-closed case in the window returns NOT_DEFINED

steps.action: Compute Reopen Rate from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.care
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 16.7% and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute Reopen Rate independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 16.7%, and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports no AI-closed case in the window returns NOT_DEFINED; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: Reopen Rate equals 16.7% for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'cases reopened within 72 hours after an AI closure' and denominator scope 'cases closed by the AI in the window'.

A recomputation that yields reopens divided by all closed cases, which dilutes a quality signal that is specifically about AI closures is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: no AI-closed case in the window returns NOT_DEFINED; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Counting a reopen that happened after 72 hours as within the window.
Counting a reopened case as a new case and losing the reopen flag.
evidence: Reopen events with the delta from the AI closure timestamp.
AI closure list used as the denominator.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for CS-05 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
